caption: What if you shouted on other planets? On Earth, your voice travels at about 343 m/s, roughly 1 km every 3 seconds. On the Moon there's no air, so there's no sound at all; astronauts talked by radio. Mars has air about 170 times thinner than ours. NASA's Perseverance rover recorded sound there at about 240 m/s, and high-pitched sounds fade so fast that two people 5 m apart would struggle to chat. Weirder still, high notes travel slightly faster on Mars, so they arrive a bit before the low ones. Venus has air about 90 times thicker and a surface over 470 °C. Scientists estimate your voice would sound deeper there. India's Venus Orbiter Mission is planned to launch in 2028. Plot twist: space isn't totally silent. A black hole in the Perseus cluster sends sound waves through hot gas, a B-flat about 57 octaves below middle C. Where would YOU shout first? 👇
